title: PXAPI analysis run state v1
description: The coarse global execution state of one Analysis Run. The vocabulary is deliberately small — CREATED, QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED — and it describes execution only. A business phase, a stage and a provider outcome are not global states and have no representation here; a stage's execution is its own record, linked to this one by run_id alone. SUCCEEDED means execution finished without failing: it does not mean customer release, delivery, report readiness, completed scoring, or legal or security approval, and it does not mean every stage succeeded. This document is the state a run is in, not a history of the states it has been in; durable transition history and replay belong to the persistence slice.

schema_version.description: Required. Always 1.0.0 for this contract. Each contract is versioned in its own right; this value is not a version of the contract set as a whole.

run_id.description: Required. The Analysis Run this state describes. It is the only link between this document and a stage execution record.

state.description: Required. The run's global execution state. The vocabulary is closed at these six values: a seventh state, a lifecycle phase name and a stage name are all rejected. Which ordered pairs are legal transitions is decided by the domain, not by this document.

entered_at.description: Required. When the run entered the state it is currently in.

finished_at.description: Conditional. Present if and only if the state is terminal — SUCCEEDED, FAILED or CANCELLED. A run that is still CREATED, QUEUED or RUNNING has not finished, so the member is absent rather than null.

code.description: Required. A stable, machine-readable code naming why execution failed. The set is open: a consumer treats a code it does not know as a generic execution failure. It is not a stage identifier and does not name the stage that failed.

failure.description: Conditional. Present if and only if the state is FAILED, and absent for every other state including CANCELLED. It carries a code and nothing else: no free text, no stage attribution and no provider detail, so a validator message, an exception or a path cannot reach a client through this member.
